steps.title: P4c-4 falls look
steps.intro: Produced by tools/render_jobs/jobs/falls_look.json at 1920x1080. A new 150 ft temperate forest map (seed 1234): a two-tier Tier step (Sculpt's Tier twice) with a straight waist river drawn from its top toward the camera along the grid, and a 13 m Raise hill east of it (an 8 m dome, its flank at 44 degrees at the steepest, a steep run of about 9 m; it stands clear of the river in screen space, since a hill between the camera and a stroke's path catches the pointer's ray) with an ankle stream drawn from its top down the flank toward the camera about 22 degrees off the grid (the angle where a grid-sampled crease saws), so P4c-1 plans two hillside falls; then a second waist river carved through the editor API (probes/water.gd carve, no pointer) from the step's top off its far edge, falling away from the camera. The carved ground is captured with the water hidden at home and at zoom 8 on each fall's foot (probes/falls.gd names them); then with the water shown at zoom 8 on every fall, close up on the tier fall at zoom 6 and 10, two zoom-10 frames about 0.25 s of shader time apart with the clock frozen for each save, Water Quality Low, and the Swamp palette; last, an indicative in-run GPU A/B of the falls mesh shown and hidden at zoom 8 (vsync off; not the pinned procedure). Judge the water (P4c-4, shaders/waterfall.gdshader): the curtain reads as falling white water with glassy streaks between, white at the lip roll, melting into the pool; the ring is a churn of foam densest at the foot, not a plate; the mist is faint spray at the pool; the streaks move between the two frames; Low drops the mist; the away-facing fall shows a white roll over its brink.
